title: Derived slice compatibility and pullback of section localizations
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R_X)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] represented by a continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and a ring map, and let $V\in\mathcal D$ with $U=u(V)$. Write $f_V$ for the induced morphism on localized ringed sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. For every $M\in D(R_X)$ and $N\in D(R_Y)$ there are canonical isomorphisms
$$j_V^*Rf_*M\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*M,\qquad j_U^*Lf^*N\cong L(f_V)^*j_V^*N.$$ 
For every section $a\in R_Y(V)$, with image $a'=f^\sharp(a)\in R_X(U)$, the second comparison identifies $L(f_V)^*(R_Y|_V[1/a])$ with $R_X|_U[1/a']$. These comparisons are natural and compatible with the derived adjunction units and counits.

proof.text: Use the ordinary ringed-site localization theorem for slice continuity and left exactness. Apply the normalized derived-image existence lemma globally and on the slice.

Choose beta from the normalized derived comparison lemma. Its inverse mate is invertible. Form lambda as that inverse mate, and obtain the counit equation from mateEquiv_counit_symm and the unit equation from unit_mateEquiv_symm followed by cancellation of lambda with its inverse. This is RingedSliceAdjunctionSquare.ofMate.

For every section use the ordinary localization-complex isomorphism from the localization-model lemma. The derived-image existence lemma computes the left-derived transformation on flat-term K-flat complexes. Apply this to the localization single complex: localizationSliceCoefficient_kflat supplies K-flatness; localization_isFlat supplies flatness in degree zero, and all other terms are zero and hence flat. Compose the counit isomorphism with Q of the ordinary localization isomorphism. Naturality of the counit at the localization-unit chain map, functoriality of Q, and the ordinary generator equation give the required derived generator equation.
